purpose: Carry each character's consequential emotional and behavioral state from one scene into the next without mutating immutable identity DNA.
core_principle: A character enters the next scene carrying the consequences of the previous scene; identity remains immutable while development state evolves.

memory_model.pipeline: trigger → memory retrieval → emotional association → belief activation → internal conflict → intention → micro-expression → body → dialogue → action
memory_model.priority: Recent consequential memories outrank generic background memories; unresolved relational events remain active until resolved, transformed, or explicitly superseded.

state_model.snapshot_rule: Scene ending state becomes the candidate entry state for the next scene.

continuity_rules: Never rewrite immutable character identity to explain a new emotion.
Every significant scene-ending event must leave a trace in the affected character state.
Do not force an old emotion to persist after its causal trigger has been resolved.
A time gap may attenuate intensity but must not erase consequential memory without an explicit narrative reason.
Emotional continuity is not identical to emotional repetition; the same event may transform into a different emotion or intention.
Relationship changes propagate only to characters causally affected by the event.
Performance changes must be explainable from retrieved memory and current objective.
Dialogue tone may change while voice identity remains locked.
Physical injury, fatigue, possession, costume damage and environmental effects are separate continuity dimensions from emotion.
A character may conceal an emotion; concealed state must remain distinct from visible performance state.
Conflicting memory records require source timestamp and confidence reconciliation before promotion.
CSD-002 receives the resolved state; it does not independently invent emotional backstory.

output_schema.character_states: per-character immutable identity + mutable entry state
output_schema.relationship_updates: affected relationship pressures and unresolved threads
output_schema.continuity_constraints: what must remain visually, emotionally and causally consistent

pass_conditions: every consequential affected character has a state transition or explicit no-change decision
visible performance is derivable from internal state

demo_test.trigger_event: Ravana voluntarily suppresses his rising power instead of escalating the confrontation.

memory_records.content: His expected dominance was interrupted by a choice to restrain himself.
Restraint may be a form of mastery rather than weakness.
Rama's controlled challenge altered Ravana's perception of the encounter.
Hanuman remained ready to intervene but accepted Rama's deliberate restraint.

state_transitions.visible_performance: quieter gaze, contained jaw tension, reduced gesture amplitude
state_transitions.next_intention: determine whether restraint increases or diminishes his authority

state_transitions.visible_performance: relaxed shoulders, steady gaze, minimal expression change
state_transitions.next_intention: allow Ravana to confront the meaning of his own choice
observe Ravana while remaining ready to protect Rama

continuity_constraints: Ravana must not revert immediately to an unqualified triumphant state.
Rama's composure must remain consistent with his established performance DNA.
Hanuman's readiness remains available even though visible threat posture decreases.
No character identity, costume or voice lock is altered by the emotional transition.

csd002_handoff.rule: Frame perspective and performance must use these resolved entry states; CSD-002 must not invent contradictory emotional motivation.
